reason: The side rails should keep the marble on the tray, directly addressing the escape problem.
expectation: I expect the rails to fit onto the tray, though the return mechanism will need more parts.

alternatives.reason: The launcher also looks necessary, but I want to secure the playing area first.

effect: The retaining rails are in place, so I can start shaping the tray for the marble's return.
reaction: That was straightforward, with no further explanation of how the rails guide the marble.
reason: The support wedge looks useful for giving the tray a slope.
expectation: I expect the wedge to tilt the tray, potentially helping the marble roll back.

alternatives.reason: The launcher needs assembling too, but I want to finish the tray first.

reaction: The slope makes sense for a gravity-driven return.
reason: I'll assemble the launcher as the only available action.
expectation: I expect the spring to fit inside the launcher and push the plunger back after use.

effect: The launcher uses a compressed spring to drive the plunger forward, with a stop limiting its push.
reaction: The explanation clarified how the launcher works; I had expected the spring to return the plunger instead.
reason: I'll attach the launcher to the sloping tray; it's the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the launcher to fit onto the tray so it can send the marble up the slope.

effect: The launcher is attached, creating a launch lane ready for a test.
reason: I'll try the marble in the table; it's the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the marble to be launched along the lane, revealing whether it returns properly.

effect: The test revealed an unwanted sideways tilt that traps the returning marble.
reaction: The corner trap gives a clear reason to adjust the table.
reason: The levelling shim is the only available combination and should correct the sideways tilt.
expectation: I expect the shim to level the tray sideways while preserving its downhill slope, though the return may still need work.

effect: The shim corrected the sideways lean, and the marble now rolls straight back to the bottom edge.
reaction: The retest clearly shows why the adjustment mattered.
reason: The catch apron is the only available combination and should keep the returning marble from rolling off.
expectation: I expect the apron to catch or guide the marble at the bottom so the player can retrieve it.

effect: The apron catches the marble, completing the return table and its goal.
reaction: The successful return is satisfying, and Jo's question makes me curious about what else the table could do.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing and levelling the tray made the effect of sideways tilt clear; the retest showed the fix working.

leastWorthwhile.text: Attaching the launcher was straightforward but offered little to think about on its own.

surprise.text: I expected the spring to return the plunger, but it actually drives the plunger forward when released.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the parts had clear purposes, though most choices were the only available action.

continue.text: Yes. The physical explanations were useful, and I'm curious what Jo might add for the marble to do on its way.
